metrics.name: effective_width_mean
metrics.provenance: 20 real samples; empty superpixels are zero-filled

thresholds.condition: conditioning_width == 48
live vec_fg numel == 48
live vec_fg shape == (1, 16, 3)
per-superpixel width from WEIGHTS == 3
LMP returns b x n x 3 (source check)
all BKRA checkpoint weights load

expected.claim: effective width on real samples = not pinned by any source

runs.revision: none -- this number has never moved
notes: PRECISION: 48 is the width of the CONDITIONING CHANNEL, not the model capacity. The U-Net is unconstrained and the retrieval codebook holds 8192 entries -- but those entries are addressed by only 48 scalars, so the bottleneck is the query side. Stating it any more broadly would overclaim.

Three INDEPENDENT confirmations, which is why this is not just a config read: the config gives the token count (16), the TRAINED WEIGHTS give the per-token width (mlp_in.fc1.weight is (6, 3), so each superpixel enters as 3 numbers), and a live forward pass of the real module on a real sample gives vec_fg = (1, 16, 3).

NEW FINDING, not in any source document: 48 is an UPPER bound. LMP zero-fills superpixels that SLIC leaves empty (ddpm.py:1558-1560), so the effective width on real samples is 45.75 on average (range 36-48 over 20 samples). The channel is at most 48 numbers wide and in practice narrower.
Code observations while reading: LMP uses no attribute of self, and its fourth argument s is dead -- sigma=5 is hardcoded at ddpm.py:1553.
Mask convention verified, not assumed: mask==1 is the region the generator invents, so 1-mask is the kept foreground, which is what LMP segments (ddpm.py:1552).

HOW THIS INTEGRATES: this is conclusion (i) of the package. With A2 (~82% of every output is invented background) it gives "we steer 82% of the picture through 48 numbers". It is also the target of the one forward path we identify -- widening this channel at ddpm.py:1579 -- so the width had to be exact.

A2.title: Object-vs-background pixel share
A2.supports: conclusion (i) - what those 48 numbers have to steer

metrics.name: primary_source
metrics.provenance: the literal inpainting mask -- the region the generator invented

thresholds.condition: invented background > 0.75
all four sources have 4447 masks
polarity rule unanimous within every source
all masks binary

notes: Binarisation threshold 127, stated because it is a choice; every mask on disk is already binary (2 unique values), so the threshold is not doing any work here.

POLARITY IS DETECTED, NOT ASSUMED. The same masks exist on disk in two polarities: LAKERED/input masks are stored with background=white (they ARE the inpainting mask), while Source/HKU-IS/GT, HKU-IS_raw/gt and LAKERED/output masks store object=white. Reading this backwards would have inverted the headline from 18% to 82%. The corner rule (corners of a salient-object mask are background) resolves it, and its agreement rate is logged per source.

CROSS-SOURCE FINDING: the LAKE-RED pipeline masks agree with Source/HKU-IS_raw/gt essentially exactly, but Source/HKU-IS/GT -- the mask set training actually reads -- differs slightly. The two GT sets are not identical, so the training source and the generation source were processed differently. Not load-bearing for A2 (both give the same ~18%), but recorded because D1 compares these same directories.

HOW THIS INTEGRATES: this is the denominator of conclusion (i). A1 gave the steering channel (<=48 scalars); A2 gives what it steers (80.8% of every image is invented). The claim is the ratio, not either number alone.

A3.title: Generated-vs-real appearance signature, with controls
A3.supports: context - demotes the AUC 0.999 finding to a truism (R-c..R-f)

metrics.name: probe_auc_darkened20
metrics.provenance: IDENTICAL images, darkened -- refutes the R-e mechanism

metrics.name: generation_recall_delta
metrics.provenance: LAKE-RED output minus its own input pool

metrics.name: fg_bg_colour_corr_authors_pool
metrics.provenance: authors' released pool (n=4447), R2 0.160 -- independent replication

thresholds.condition: embedder reproduces the cached features (min cos >= 0.999)
real-vs-real RANDOM split is a genuine null (AUC < 0.60)
the sorted-filename split is NOT a null (AUC > 0.75) -- the R-c bug
JPEG-75 alone reaches AUC > 0.85, so 0.999 is near-vacuous
two ordinary different datasets reach AUC > 0.95 -- the surviving support for R-f
the fg->bg colour sign flip replicates in the AUTHORS pool too
darkening does NOT separate (AUC < 0.60) -- R-e retraction
generation REDUCES recall vs its own input pool
corrected ceiling exceeds the buggy one

expected.claim: probe AUC real vs raw HKU-IS = 0.9831

runs.revision: R-c sorted-filename split bug (ceiling 0.893/0.871 -> corrected, both computed here); R-d recall share 54% -> recomputed; R-e ~20-level darkening RETRACTED as the mechanism; R-f AUC 0.999 demoted to near-vacuous
notes: THIS EXPERIMENT DEMOTES OUR OWN HEADLINE, which is why it is in the package. AUC 0.9989 real-vs-generated looks damning until the controls sit beside it: JPEG-75 recompression of the IDENTICAL images reaches 0.4117, and two ordinary different datasets reach 0.9831. AUC 0.999 establishes only "these are different distributions", which nobody disputes. A reviewer would have dismissed it.
The protocol itself is sound -- the true null (random real-vs-real split) lands at 0.4781, i.e. chance.

GATE: this script re-embeds 8 target images and requires cos >= 0.999 against the cached vectors before mixing fresh control features with cached ones (measured 0.99999). The original preprocessing was never saved and had to be recovered by testing eight candidate pipelines; the winner is PIL Resize((224,224)) BICUBIC with no crop, ImageNet normalisation, CLS token stored unnormalised. Near-misses were dangerous: Resize+CenterCrop gives 0.978 and cv2.INTER_AREA gives 0.997, so a reasonable-looking pipeline would have silently produced slightly wrong features.

R-c REPRODUCED, NOT JUST DESCRIBED: the original "null control" split the target features in sorted-filename order, which put COD10K on one side and CAMO on the other. This script computes that split too -- AUC 0.8888 and ceiling 0.893/0.871 -- beside the corrected random split (0.4781, 0.941/0.937). Both are logged so the defect is visible.

R-e RETRACTED: darkening the identical images by 20 levels gives AUC 0.3469. DINOv2 is essentially invariant to that shift, so background darkening cannot be the mechanism behind the style axis. The earlier mechanistic claim is withdrawn.

THE RESULT THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS is panel 3, and it points the opposite way from the original framing: LAKE-RED does not merely have LIMITED coverage of the target manifold, it DESTROYS coverage its own input already had. Raw HKU-IS recall 0.746 -> LAKE-RED 0.466, a 37.5% relative loss, bought for +0.041 precision.

HOW THIS INTEGRATES: A3 supports none of the four load-bearing conclusions. It removes two claims we should not lean on, and reframes the style gap as a CONSEQUENCE -- it is why coverage-counting is inverse-ranked by feasibility, which B2 measures directly as rho(acceptance, n_s) = +0.73..+0.92.

Limitations: JPEG quality 75 and darkening 20 levels are the audit's specific control settings, not a sweep. k=5 for the manifold estimate. Precision/recall is computed on L2-normalised features; the sources did not state whether they normalised, so this is our stated choice.

B1.title: ES-vs-true-error correlation
B1.supports: SURVIVED - uncertainty is a real weakness signal

metrics.name: crossrun_ES_scale_spread
metrics.provenance: only the RANKING is portable, not any absolute threshold

thresholds.condition: all checkpoint tensors copied (CHECKPOINT_LOADING_BUG.md)
image/GT pairing aligned by stem in both splits
self-check: mean MAE within 0.001 of the recorded 0.0745
self-check: mean Sa within 0.005 of the recorded 0.7172
regenerated predictions match the recorded ones (mean |d| < 1 level)
per-image ES matches the audit's own scores (r > 0.999)
ES predicts per-cluster MAE at rho > 0.75 (test, k=20)
ES predicts per-cluster MAE on VAL too, perm p < 0.05
the MAE correlation replicates across runs (sd < 0.10)
ES ranking agrees between every pair of runs (rho > 0.70)
R-h: ES predicts Sa MORE WEAKLY than MAE

expected.claim: self-check mean MAE vs the audit's stored per-image scores = 0.074463
self-check mean MAE vs the repo's recorded value = 0.0745
self-check mean Sa vs the repo's recorded value = 0.7172

runs.revision: R-h: rho 0.82 is against MAE; against the headline metric Sa the same signal gives only +0.40..+0.65. Both computed here.
notes: WHAT SURVIVED. ES-disagreement is a genuine weakness signal: rho +0.788 against per-cluster MAE at k=20 on test, replicating at +0.893 +/- 0.059 across 5 INDEPENDENT training runs, with the ES-based cluster RANKING -- the quantity d(c) actually consumes -- agreeing between every pair of runs at rho +0.765..+0.911. This is not a single-run artifact.

R-h, THE SCOPE CORRECTION, computed here rather than asserted: against the headline metric Sa the same signal gives only +0.409 (k=20) and +0.442 (k=50) per-cluster, and +0.311 per-image. So rho=0.82 licenses "ES ranks clusters by pixel-calibration error"; it does NOT license "ES predicts the error that matters". Note what is NOT recipe-sensitive: every per-image value and every cross-run value reproduces EXACTLY, because neither needs clustering.

THE CONCLUSION IS ROBUST TO THE RECIPE, which is what matters: rho(ES, MAE) stays in +0.788..+0.949 at k=20 and +0.826..+0.878 at k=50 across all four variants, and R-h holds under all four -- the weakest MAE correlation (+0.788) still exceeds the strongest Sa correlation (+0.624).
